purpose: Auditable ledger of the Local2 P0 closure. Every entry is falsifiable: commit SHAs are checked against the repository, test counts against a re-run, and statuses against the vocabulary in section 21 of the closure spec.

phases.title: Read/Search Navigation
evidence: file.read gains start_line and a hard 8000-line ceiling enforced identically on both dispatch paths
file.search gains max_results, context_before/after and deterministic ordering via rg --sort path
the fast path previously passed max_lines straight to the renderer, so max_lines=1e7 returned the whole file on one path and 8000 lines on the other

phases.title: Test/Build Execution
evidence: ExecutionFailureClass.TEST_SUITE_FAILED separates a tool reporting a verdict from a process misbehaving, scoped by tool rather than by exit code
test.run no longer infers the runner from what is installed; the fallback is gated on project ecosystem markers and otherwise fails closed
declared runtime versus actual runtime is an execution admission gate; ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH refuses with no execution_id

phases.title: Process Lifecycle
evidence: stdout_truncated and stderr_truncated now travel from direct_exec into ExecutionRecord and to_public; previously the flags were computed and discarded
is_terminal is exposed so callers need not hardcode the terminal set
START to RUNNING to COMPLETE, FAILED and CANCELLED are each observed on a real subprocess

findings.summary: A cancel issued while an execution is still STARTING returns ok=true and leaves the command running to COMPLETED, because there is no process group to signal yet.
findings.why_open: Cancelling after RUNNING does reach CANCELLED, which P0-H qualifies. The pre-RUNNING window is unproven and is a lifecycle question, not a WIP one.
findings.evidence: veya/remote/execution.py cancel(): os.killpg is guarded by if record.process_group_id

phases.title: Security / Permission / Sandbox
evidence: five escape routes refused with no execution_id and no tool reached: parent traversal, /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, a sibling directory, and a symlink pointing outside
UNKNOWN resolves to UNKNOWN and is refused at the tool boundary with TOOL_DENIED; it is deliberately outside EFFECT_LATTICE
the four authorities hold none of each other's verdicts

phases.title: WIP Preservation
evidence: a governed file.write lands under .veya/worktrees/ and the canonical file is never created
staged index, unstaged set, untracked files, HEAD and branch survive a write, a refusal, a failing execution and a cancel
session-level content-hash comparison: every tracked modification and all 13 untracked files byte-identical across the phase

findings.summary: Spec 10.3 asks for an isolated worktree by default for tests. On main that holds for mutation only: read and execute intent default to CANONICAL_WORKTREE, so a command that writes writes into the owner's live tree.
findings.why_open: The resolver documents the reason, and it is defensible: a fresh worktree is a clean checkout with no virtualenv and none of the current working state, so running there made the tree's own modules unimportable. This is a spec-versus-implementation divergence and an architecture decision, escalated rather than accepted or fixed.
findings.evidence: veya/remote/tool_adapter.py resolve_execution_target rule 4 and its comment; measured by tests/remote/test_p0j_wip_preservation.py::test_a_writing_command_pollutes_the_canonical_tree

blockers.summary: runtime.coding.tools.coding_worktree_create fails in this environment with: module 'oskill' has no attribute 'capability_intersection'.
blockers.workaround: WorktreeManager is used directly so the adapter's isolation and identity verification remain under test.
blockers.owner: harness work already in flight in the working tree

phases.title: Full Local Development E2E
evidence: The explicit isolated-execution gate WORKS: test.run with execution_target=NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE reports target_type NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE, executes with cwd set to .veya/worktrees/task-*, and the command's own os.getcwd() independently matches the record's cwd.
Canonical HEAD, the modified tracked file and canonical source contents were all byte-identical across that run, so P0-J-F1 has a working remedy available even though the default stays canonical.
The sequence cannot be carried past the repair step because main has no commit surface: the git.* tools are git.status, git.diff, git.log and git.promote only.
veya/remote/git_promotion.py states 'Promotion != Commit: changes remain in working tree/index; NO auto-commit, NO auto-push', and git.promote requires an execution_id whose commit already exists.

blockers.summary: No git.stage and no git.commit exist in the governed surface, so acceptance steps 13-18 (stage, commit, verify commit, promote) cannot be executed.
blockers.why_blocked: The only route would be shell.exec running git add/git commit, which is the bypass the closure spec forbids, or adding a commit capability, which is an architecture change rather than a qualification.
blockers.evidence: BINDINGS git.* == [git.status, git.diff, git.log, git.promote]; runtime/coding has no coding_*commit* function
blockers.owner: requires an architecture decision before P0-L can run

phases.title: Full Local Development E2E (rerun)
evidence: Steps A-M are reachable on the governed surface: the explicit NEW_ISOLATED_WORKTREE target resolves, file.read/file.search are bounded against it, file.write lands in the worktree, test.run produces a real TEST_SUITE_FAILED then a real pass after a governed repair, build.run runs for real, and git.stage/git.commit produce a commit whose SHA matches an independent git rev-parse.
git.stage and git.commit are bound to coding_git_stage and coding_git_commit and route through WorktreeManager, so P0-M's authority topology holds.
Canonical HEAD, branch and tracked file contents are unchanged throughout, so WIP preservation holds.

git.verify does not exist in the governed surface (git.* is status, diff, stage, commit, log, promote) and P0-M did not add it, so the verify step named by the rerun spec has no governed implementation.

blockers.summary: Step M (Git Verify) names git.verify, which does not exist as a governed tool. Adding it is outside the rerun's permitted change set.
blockers.why_blocked: Section 46 freezes the governed git surface. Verification could only be done with the git CLI as an independent oracle, which is a reinterpretation of the spec rather than the spec's letter.
blockers.evidence: BINDINGS git.* == [git.status, git.diff, git.stage, git.commit, git.log, git.promote]

blockers.summary: Sections 24 and 25 require the whole lifecycle to belong to one durable GoalRun and to end in a Verifier ACCEPT, but the governed tools this rerun must use are direct RemoteToolAdapter jobs with no Verifier.
blockers.why_blocked: ExecutionRecord carries goal_run_id and task_id but has no verifier field at all, and the direct command flow does not populate a GoalRun. The only GoalRun-attached governed path is worker.dispatch, which requires an LLM worker binary and is unavailable here. Wiring a Verifier into the direct path is outside the permitted change set.
blockers.evidence: ExecutionRecord has no field matching 'verif'; set_effect_receipt/EffectReceipt is reached only from worker.dispatch

blockers.summary: Section 23 makes a structured-receipt defect a BLOCKED condition, and TOOL-BUG-1 is still open.
blockers.why_blocked: set_finalization_evidence still assigns record.effect_receipt only when isinstance(receipt, dict), with no else branch, so a stringified receipt is silently discarded. Section 3.6 forbids fixing it in this phase.

target_contract.reason: TargetContract does not exist on main. It is present only on local2/l0-l1-l2. Per spec section 3 no phase may claim convergence, and redoing P0-B/P0-E on main is forbidden.

tool_bug_1.summary: A non-dict effect receipt is silently discarded rather than rejected, so a receipt that arrives stringified is indistinguishable from no receipt at all.
tool_bug_1.evidence: veya/remote/execution.py set_finalization_evidence assigns record.effect_receipt only when isinstance(receipt, dict); there is no else branch and no diagnostic.
tool_bug_1.why_not_closed: Fixing it changes finalizer evidence handling on a governed path and needs its own qualification. Closing it by asserting the schema would be exactly the fake evidence this phase exists to prevent.

mutations_green_then_repaired.cause: the containment check had no test anywhere in the suite
mutations_green_then_repaired.repair: added two negative tests plus a positive counter-test, re-ran RED

mutations_green_then_repaired.cause: every assertion was made against a record that genuinely was terminal
mutations_green_then_repaired.repair: asserted is_terminal is False on an observed running record, re-ran RED

baseline_failures_untouched.note: Isolated per spec section 24 and not re-baselined. runtime 24 failed / 505 passed and goalrun 1 failed / 200 passed have failure sets byte-identical to the pre-P0 measurement.

closure_gate.reason: P0-L remains BLOCKED after the P0-M rerun. Three blockers stand: git.verify absent, no Verifier or GoalRun attachment on the direct path, and TOOL-BUG-1 open under section 23. Local2 local development closure cannot be declared COMPLETE. Integration remains deferred.

wip_preservation.method: content-hash comparison before and after every phase
wip_preservation.forbidden_operations_used: none: no git clean, no git reset, no git stash at any point in P0-F through P0-K
